_comment: Single source of truth for the unit and item sheet column layouts.
Before this file the same three maps were written out by hand in read_workbook.js,
read_workbook.py and save_config.py, and they had drifted: read_workbook.py was missing
do160_applies, software_control_category and worst_case_severity, so a build run through the
legacy Python reader (ISAF_USE_PYTHON_READER=1) silently dropped three columns the customer
had filled in. Every consumer now reads this file, so a column can only be added in one place.
This lives in 07_Web_Service because it must survive edition packaging: 03_Build_Engine/src is
stripped from Customer and Demo apps (scripts/make_edition.py) while save_config.py ships and
needs these maps at runtime. esbuild inlines the import into build.bundle.js, so the build
order matters: readListRows takes columns[0] as the column that ends the table, and moves pn to
index 2 when a workbook has the PN shim. Keep the declared order when editing.
readKey renames a column on read only, where the reader normalizes the raw cell into a typed
value under the plain key (do160_applies_raw -> boolean do160_applies).
See 00_Docs/developer/UNIT_HIERARCHY_DESIGN.md. Adding a field here is step 1 of that design:
item ata_chapter, multi-parent parent_system and technology scoping all edit this file.
_fixedColumns: fixedColumns is per sheet, not global. A column added after the PN shim must keep the same
letter in a workbook with PN in column C and in one without, so it never rides the shift. The
letter differs by sheet because the sheets are different widths, and ata_chapter now appears on
all three: K on Systems, N on Software Items, M on Hardware Items. Each is one past the last
column that sheet uses in BOTH layouts - Systems ends at J/K, Software at M, Hardware at L -
so a fixed letter is safe in either. A global map cannot express this: ata_chapter would collide
with software_control_category and do160_applies, which both sit at K on their own sheets.
Every consumer passes the sheet's own map: read_workbook.js/.py, workbook_comments.js,
_unitType: unit_type and parent_unit, added 16 November 2026, give the Sys/LRU sheet two levels instead of
one. A row says what it is - SYSTEM or LRU - and an LRU names the system that contains it.
Blank unit_type keeps a row behaving exactly as before, so an untouched workbook is unchanged:
every existing row is simply a unit, which is what the single level already meant.
One tab with a type column rather than a separate LRU tab (owner, 15 November 2026): a System row
and an LRU row want nearly the same fields, and ARP4754 lets a system decompose into subsystems
before reaching LRUs, which two fixed tabs could not express. Items attach by id through
parent_system either way, so the item sheets are unaffected.
L and M are past everything the sheet uses in both layouts (A-J plus fixed K), so they are pinned
for the same reason ata_chapter is.
_articleCharacteristics: Article characteristics for the Declaration of Design and Performance, added 16 November 2026.
They sit on the Sys/LRU sheet because they describe the ARTICLE - the certifiable unit - not the
program and not an item inside it. AMC 21.A.608 items 2, 3 and 9(b)-9(e).
NONE IS MANDATORY and a blank cell is not an omission: most apply to some articles only. A DC-DC
converter neither transmits nor measures. A blank renders as 'Not applicable' in the DDP rather
than as a placeholder, so a reviewer can tell an answered question from an unanswered one.
They are fields rather than document placeholders at the owner's direction: adding them now costs
one migration, while adding them later would change the customer app a second time.
tso_numbers is a LIST. One article can hold several authorizations at once - a display meeting
TSO-C113b, TSO-C115d and TSO-C153a on one nameplate - so the DDP prints the full set.
N through U are past everything the sheet uses in both layouts, so they are pinned like the rest.
